precepts.text: The officers released the man with a new house, a new vineyard, a new wife, and the fearful man, lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart.
precepts.point: The Most High chose able men. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred; and when Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

precepts.why:
The book of Numbers is the numbering of the armies of the Lord, the armies of the children of Israel: every male “From twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war in Israel.” Every man went to war unless the law released him, and this is the law that released him.

The officers spoke to the people before the battle. “What man is there that hath built a new house, and hath not dedicated it? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.” The same for the man that “hath planted a vineyard, and hath not yet eaten of it”, and for the man that “hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her”: let him go and return unto his house. A man that had newly married, or built a house and not dedicated it, did not have to go.

Then the officers spoke further: “What man is there that is fearful and fainthearted? let him go and return unto his house, lest his brethren’s heart faint as well as his heart.” The fearful man did not have to go either, because that spirit of fear would jump on the other brothers. The armies numbered in Numbers 1 were the able men, and the Most High chose able men.

precepts.text: The nations have said, come, and let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance; this is the battle Israel is in now.
precepts.point: Fear makes people trim their ways: afraid of family at the pagan holiday table, tucking their fringes in certain places, scared to be seen in the truth. Stand boldly; the Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, for that spirit came from Satan himself.

note.label: Deuteronomy 20: Laws of Warfare and the Spirit of Fear

precepts.why:
“When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them”. That goes for us now, because we are still in a battle. The psalm names it: “They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.”

The nations are confederate against Israel being a nation any more and against our remembrance of Israel and our laws. We are not physically out battling the nations as our forefathers were when they took the land; we are in a spiritual battle, and this whole world is set up for our people to go into sin and iniquity.

That is the people more than thou we face, and the word stands: be not afraid of them, for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

precepts.text: Though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh; the weapons of our warfare are not carnal but mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds, the doctrines, lusts, and wicked thoughts in the minds of our people, fought with the scriptures, the sword of truth.
precepts.point: Fear makes people trim their ways: afraid of family at the pagan holiday table, tucking their fringes in certain places, scared to be seen in the truth. Stand boldly; the Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, for that spirit came from Satan himself.

note.label: Deuteronomy 20: Laws of Warfare and the Spirit of Fear

precepts.why:
What kind of battle is Israel in now? “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)”.

We are not physically out battling the nations as our forefathers were when they took the land; we are in a spiritual battle. The strongholds are the doctrines, lusts, and wicked thoughts in the minds of our people, and they are fought with the scriptures, the sword of truth.

The nations are confederate against Israel being a nation any more, and this whole world is set up for our people to go into sin and iniquity. So the horses and chariots and the people more than thou are met today with weapons mighty through God, not carnal ones, and the word is the same: be not afraid of them.

precepts.text: God hath not given us the spirit of fear; do not be afraid in this battle.
precepts.point: Fear makes people trim their ways: afraid of family at the pagan holiday table, tucking their fringes in certain places, scared to be seen in the truth. Stand boldly; the Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, for that spirit came from Satan himself.

note.label: Deuteronomy 20: Laws of Warfare and the Spirit of Fear

precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” Moses said be not afraid of them, and Paul says the same: do not be afraid in this battle.

Fear makes people trim their ways: afraid of family at the pagan holiday table, tucking their fringes in certain places, scared to be seen in the truth. Stand boldly. The Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, for that spirit came from Satan himself; what he gave is power, love, and a sound mind.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
precepts.point: A lot of times you do not see that the Lord is fighting for you in the spirit; that is where faith comes in, for the Bible is a faith-based book. You have to have faith that the Most High is fighting for you, with angels encamped round about the righteous, as David told us.

note.label: Deuteronomy 20: Laws of Warfare and the Spirit of Fear

precepts.why:
The priest told Israel at the battle: let not your hearts faint, fear not, do not tremble, neither be ye terrified, “For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”

A lot of times you do not see that the Lord is fighting for you in the spirit; that is where faith comes in, for the Bible is a faith-based book. David told us how he fights for us: “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

You have to have faith that the Most High is fighting for you, with angels encamped round about the righteous, even when you cannot see them. That is the one that goeth with you to save you.

precepts.text: When thou goest out to battle, be not afraid, for the Lord thy God is with thee.
precepts.point: The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
The war laws give the same understanding as the new wife's year at home. “When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.”

The Lord is the one with the host when it goes to battle; the battle does not hang on the one man newly married. So he is not sent out to war, and is not charged with any business; he is free at home one year.

precepts.text: The Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.
precepts.point: The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
“For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.” Because the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies, men could be sent home before the battle.

“What man is there that hath built a new house, and hath not dedicated it? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.” The man with a new house is sent back, and the same words send back the man that had betrothed a wife. It is the same understanding as the new husband not going out to war: the Lord fights, and the man is kept for his house and his wife.

precepts.text: What man hath betrothed a wife and not taken her? let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.
precepts.point: The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
“And what man is there that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her? let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her.” The war laws give the same understanding as this law.

The man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her; the man that has taken a new wife shall not go out to war at all, but be free at home one year to cheer up his wife. Both stand on the same ground: the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies, so the man is not needed at the battle and is kept for his wife.

precepts.text: The law of war: far-off cities that answer peace become tributaries, but of the cities of these nations save alive nothing that breatheth.
precepts.point: Genesis 15:13 is not talking about America. Judah has been here longer than four hundred years and the northern kingdom longer than six hundred, so this is not us coming up out of Babylon the great; and Israel was actually in Egypt four hundred and thirty years, free for the first thirty.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
There is a law pertaining to war: “When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it. And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.” If it will make no peace, thou shalt besiege it, smite every male with the edge of the sword, and take the women, the little ones, the cattle and the spoil unto thyself.

But that applied to cities very far off: “Thus shalt thou do unto all the cities which are very far off from thee, which are not of the cities of these nations. But of the cities of these people, which the Lord thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth: But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee”.

That is why at Hazor “there was not any left to breathe”, and in all the cities of those kings every man they smote with the edge of the sword, taking only the spoil and the cattle for a prey. As the Lord commanded Moses, so did Moses command Joshua, and so did Joshua; he left nothing undone.

precepts.text: Be not afraid of horses and chariots and a people more than thou, for the Lord thy God is with thee.
precepts.point: Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
The law of war opens with courage: “When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.”

Israel had no reason to leave these nations standing and dwell among them. Even against horses and chariots and a people more than thou, the Most High was with them. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
The law of war made a different stipulation for far off cities than for these people. For the far cities: “When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it. And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.” That is just what we read the tribes doing with the Canaanites, putting them to tribute.

If the city would not make peace, “thou shalt besiege it: And when the Lord thy God hath delivered it into thine hands, thou shalt smite every male thereof with the edge of the sword.”

But that was the rule for far off cities. For the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites that Israel is now dwelling among, there was no offer of peace and no tribute; read on to verse 16.

precepts.text: But of the cities of these people thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth, that they teach you not to do after all their abominations.
precepts.point: Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Here is the stipulation for the very people Israel dwelt among: “But of the cities of these people, which the Lord thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth: But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee.” Total destruction, not peace and not tribute.

The reason is the very thing Judges 3 records happening: “That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should ye sin against the Lord your God.” Israel saved them alive, dwelt among them, married their daughters, “and served their gods.” The children of Israel “did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves”, exactly the sin the commandment was given to prevent.

precepts.text: When thou goest out to battle and seest a people more than thou, be not afraid of them, for the Lord thy God is with thee; the priest was to tell the people, let not your hearts faint, fear not, for the Lord your God goeth with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.
precepts.point: The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle: “When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” The priest was to tell the people, “let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them; For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”

This fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith. The same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them.

precepts.point: Let this be the reward of my adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul. The adversaries are the nations, and the Lord fights for us against our enemies to save us.

note.label: Psalm 109: Give Myself unto Prayer

precepts.why:
“Let this be the reward of mine adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul.” The reward comes from the Lord, because the Lord fights for us: “For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”

The adversaries are the nations, and the Lord goes with us to fight against them, to save us.
